title: Private AI Readiness Kit
subtitle: A five-minute hardware audit, privacy boundary, and model-fit test to decide whether local AI makes sense on the computer you already own.
eyebrow: Schep Digital · Free Local AI Starter

intro_callout.title: Do this before downloading a model
intro_callout.body: Local AI can reduce cloud exposure and subscription dependence, but only when the machine, model, interface, files, and network path fit the job. This kit helps you make that decision before spending time or money.

chapters.title: Define the job first
chapters.sub: A model is only useful when it passes a real task.

blocks.text: Do not begin with a leaderboard or a parameter count. Write down one repeatable task you want to keep local: summarizing private notes, drafting from confidential source material, extracting fields from documents, or coding without sending a repository to a third party. Your task determines the quality, context, speed, and privacy requirements.

items: Name one task you currently perform at least weekly.
Choose a non-sensitive sample that represents the real work.
Define a pass condition: required facts, output format, and maximum waiting time.
Decide whether the task truly needs offline or local-only processing.
List any tools, web search, cloud storage, or browser extensions the workflow would still use.

blocks.label: Write your acceptance target
blocks.text:
TASK: [one repeatable job]
SOURCE: [non-sensitive test material]
PASS WHEN: [facts and format required]
TOO SLOW WHEN: [your maximum wait]
MUST STAY LOCAL: [files or information that cannot leave the machine]

blocks.title: Local is a design choice
blocks.body: A model can run locally while a connected tool, synced folder, browser interface, or exposed network port still sends data elsewhere. Judge the complete workflow, not the model file alone.

chapters.title: Audit the machine you own
chapters.sub: Record usable resources before choosing a model.

blocks.text: Model weights need memory, and the runtime needs additional headroom for context and processing. Longer context, multiple loaded models, vision input, and concurrent requests increase memory use. Treat a model's download size as a lower-bound signal, not a guarantee that it will run well.

rows: System memory
Task Manager, Activity Monitor, or free -h
Sets the practical ceiling for CPU or unified-memory use
GPU and VRAM
Performance view, System Information, or GPU tools
Determines whether useful acceleration fits with headroom
Free storage
Operating-system storage settings
Models, updates, and caches need room
Operating system
System/About screen
Must match the current runner's supported release
Normal workload
Memory use with everyday apps open
A test that only works after closing everything may not be useful

items: Write down total memory and normal idle memory use.
Record the exact GPU model and available VRAM when present.
Confirm enough free storage for the model plus working headroom.
Start with one small quantized text model and one request at a time.
Reject any setup that causes constant swapping, instability, or unusable heat and latency.

blocks.title: The practical rule
blocks.body: Keep the smallest model that passes your real task. A larger model that is too slow or disruptive to use has zero practical quality.

chapters.title: Draw the privacy boundary
chapters.sub: Verify every place data can travel.

blocks.text: Private local AI is a chain. The model runner, optional browser interface, connected tools, document folders, telemetry settings, and network binding all affect the result. Review the chain before introducing sensitive material.

items: Model and runner: obtain them from official sources and review their current documentation.
Interface: check analytics, update checks, remote connectors, and optional cloud providers.
Tools: disable web search, external APIs, and remote functions unless the task requires them.
Files: keep sensitive source material out of folders synchronized to a cloud service.
Network: bind services locally unless remote access is intentional and secured.
Test: disconnect the network after setup and repeat a non-sensitive task.
Verification: do not claim compliance from a local install alone; apply your own security and legal review.

rows: Runner
Does inference work after the network is disconnected?
Interface
Is any analytics or cloud provider enabled?
Files
Is the working folder synchronized elsewhere?
Tools
Can a prompt trigger an external request?
Network
Can another device reach the local service?

blocks.title: Use test data first
blocks.body: Prove the complete path with non-sensitive material. Only introduce confidential work after the boundary behaves as intended.

chapters.title: Run one repeatable fit test
chapters.sub: Measure the setup instead of guessing.

items: Close unusually heavy applications so the baseline is repeatable.
Run the same 150–300 word test prompt three times.
Record time to first response, total response time, and whether the output passes.
Inspect the runtime's CPU/GPU allocation while the model is loaded.
Repeat once with the network disconnected after all required files are installed.
Keep, downsize, or reject the model based on the task—not hype.

blocks.label: Reusable acceptance prompt
blocks.text:
TASK
Summarize the SOURCE in exactly five bullets.

RULES
- Use only facts present in SOURCE.
- If a requested fact is absent, write: Not provided.
- Keep each bullet under 25 words.
- After the bullets, list ambiguous claims.

SOURCE
[paste 150–300 words of non-sensitive test text]

rows: Passes and feels responsive
Keep it; test the real workflow cautiously
Passes but is too slow
Try a smaller or more compressed model
Fast but misses required facts
Improve the task brief, then test a better-fit model
Works only with unsafe shortcuts
Reject the setup and redesign the boundary
